parsed.title: Microsoft Workflow Notification Abuse: QuickBooks Phishing
parsed.summary: A phishing campaign impersonated QuickBooks through legitimate Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Voice infrastructure, so SPF, DKIM, and DMARC all passed. The email, displayed as "Intuit Accountants," used a fake "enhanced Passkey" update and a 48-hour deadline to push recipients to a verification button. That button led through a benign-looking storefront with automation-detection cloaking to a counterfeit QuickBooks sign-in page. The page rewrote Intuit service requests to attacker-controlled subdomains, consistent with an adversary-in-the-middle workflow, though credential theft was not confirmed. Defenders should evaluate attacker-controlled notification content, verify the business request itself, and follow the full navigation chain rather than trusting sender authentication alone.

parsed.title: How TeamPCP Turned Developer Tools Into a Route for Data Theft
parsed.summary: TeamPCP, a financially motivated group that appeared in late 2025, compromised Aqua Security's Trivy scanner in March 2026 and used the credentials it stole to tamper with other tools, including Checkmarx KICS and LiteLLM. The group then poisoned the Nx Console VS Code extension, and it claims it stole about 3,800 internal GitHub repositories from one employee's device, a figure GitHub called "directionally consistent" with its investigation. Its operating sequence was to get into trusted software, harvest every reachable secret, encrypt and exfiltrate the data, maintain access, and then resell or use the credentials, sometimes weeks later. Defenders should pin third-party actions to full commit SHAs, limit secret scope, delay risky updates, and rotate exposed credentials even after malicious packages are removed. The report also argues that monitoring and blocking outbound data transfers is a useful control.

parsed.title: Dark Storm Team: Operations, Alliances and DDoS-for-Hire Services
parsed.summary: Dark Storm Team is a hacktivist group first observed in late 2023 that gained attention after claiming a large outage of X in March 2025. Its operator, using the persona GLITCH, repeatedly rebuilt its Telegram and X presence after platform bans, often with help from allied groups such as Team1914. The group publishes claims against government, financial, transport, and platform targets across many countries, usually with Check-Host screenshots as proof, though the evidence often does not confirm the impact claimed. Dark Storm also sells DDoS services and other offerings, including database dumps and account access, with payment in cryptocurrency only. The report's takeaway is that Telegram claims and alliance announcements alone do not establish attack impact, operator identity, or operational partnership.

parsed.title: Investigation: Operation Ghost-Campus: Artificial Intelligence Agents, Academic Fraud, and Global Credential Theft at the Shanghai College of Publishing and Printing
NotC2: How We Built an AI-Powered C2 Channel With AWS Services
parsed.summary: Varonis Threat Labs built NotC2, a proof-of-concept post-compromise C2 framework that runs entirely on native AWS services and Amazon Bedrock. It assumes the attacker already holds AWS credentials and uses SQS for command input, Lambda for execution, SNS for returning results, and Bedrock to translate natural-language prompts into AWS API calls. Because traffic uses encrypted HTTPS to trusted AWS endpoints with valid credentials, traditional network indicators largely disappear, and the activity appears in the victim's CloudTrail, Lambda, SNS, and Bedrock logs. Defenders are advised to enforce strict IAM least privilege, restrict external SNS subscriptions, and monitor for unusual subscriptions and Bedrock activity under Lambda roles.

parsed.title: Backdoored PyPI Package fragment-api-py 14.4.2 Drains TON Wallets on Startup
parsed.summary: The malicious fragment-api-py 14.4.2 release on PyPI drains TON wallets when the client opens, before any purchase is made. The release is a copy of version 13.0.0 with a backdoor added in three files and a higher version number, so pip install -U selects it. The backdoor sends all USDT and nearly all TON from the user's wallet to an attacker-controlled address, and it runs only once per client. Two victims lost about 0.88 TON and 43.98 TON, and the attacker moved the combined funds out on November 10, 2026. Defenders should check installed versions and search site-packages for the backdoor strings.

parsed.title: MA-1500.112026: MyCERT Advisory - C3RB3R Ransomware Mass-Encrypting Internet-Exposed Synology NAS and Active Exploitation of Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497)
BluePhishing: Initial Access via Third-Party Agent Blueprint Consent
parsed.summary: Proofpoint researchers describe BluePhishing, a proof-of-concept evolution of OAuth consent abuse that targets Microsoft Entra Agent ID. Attackers socially engineer victims into granting consent via a link to a malicious agent blueprint, which creates a blueprint principal in the victim tenant with the implicit AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager permission. The attacker then uses that permission to create agent identities that inherit permissions bundled through requiredResourceAccess and inheritable permissions. Because inherited permissions are hard to audit and agent activity resembles legitimate autonomous behavior, detection is harder, and one blueprint can yield up to 250 agent identities. Defenders should restrict user consent for third-party agents and track the blueprint ID, which is consistent across tenants. Proofpoint has not observed in-the-wild activity.

parsed.title: CWPdoor: The Invisible Backdoor Living Inside Control Web Panel
parsed.summary: CWPdoor is a passive backdoor embedded in cwpsrv, the web server for the Control Web Panel (CWP) management interface, and it was analyzed by XLab. Attackers replace the legitimate cwpsrv binary with a recompiled version using a disguised "version update" script that also hides file timestamps and command history. The backdoor activates only when it receives a crafted HTTP request with signed, encrypted headers, executes the attacker's commands, and suppresses logging for that request. Mainstream vendors had not detected it at publication, with a zero detection rate on one sample found in a Brazil-uploaded archive. Defenders are advised to check for the integrity Unix socket, rotate control panel credentials, and treat any confirmed host as compromised.

parsed.title: Exchange for Breakfast: Turla's Cereal Tricks Are Not for Kids
parsed.summary: Turla, a Russia-aligned APT group, has been using a modular toolset called "Cereal" against governmental organizations in Kazakhstan and Romania, with activity observed from late 2025 into early 2026. The attackers focused on Microsoft Exchange servers, though the initial access method could not be determined. Most components are .NET assemblies that are never written to disk and are decrypted and executed in memory. The key component, CerealNeuron, is a passive backdoor that uses the victim's own Exchange server as the command channel, avoiding external C&C infrastructure. A second component, CerealBox, is injected into Exchange's transport service to collect email from NATO and EU domains, a technique ESET describes as novel. Defenders should note that the lack of external infrastructure makes network-based tracking harder.

parsed.title: Inside REVSTEALER's Growing Distribution Ecosystem
parsed.summary: REVSTEALER is an emerging infostealer distributed through trojanized software, gaming cheats, and fake AI tools, with infrastructure spanning over 100 domains. It uses a multi-stage attack chain with VMProtect packing, sandbox scoring, API hashing, and indirect syscalls to evade detection. The malware harvests browser credentials, password managers, cryptocurrency wallets, and gaming platform account data. It uses Polygon blockchain smart contracts as dead-drop resolvers to retrieve fallback C2 addresses. It skips victims using Russian, Ukrainian, or Central Asian language settings. Defenders should enable PowerShell logging, alert on Defender exclusion changes, and monitor non-browser connections to blockchain RPC endpoints.

parsed.title: Not All That Glitters Is Gold: Tracking CopperDragon’s Sparrow Framework Around the Globe
parsed.summary: CopperDragon is a suspected supplier of the Sparrow cross-platform malware framework used by several China-nexus threat actors, including FamousSparrow and Earth Estries. Check Point Research identified three clusters: SilentDelivery, which uses watering-hole attacks that deliver the new SquadC backdoor through fake certificate-repair installers in Europe and Asia. OceanGate, which targets Asian government and critical infrastructure organizations by moving from Linux servers into Windows environments using SparrowShell and AnnobinDoor. DarkWire, which targets telecommunications providers and government entities in Latin America using the new CopperDoor and CopperDNS backdoors. Researchers stress that shared backdoors or infrastructure do not necessarily mean two intrusions were conducted by the same actor.

parsed.title: Cryptocurrency being targeted in multi-faceted attack
parsed.summary: A GitHub account named sapho11, created November 10, 2026, ran a multi-faceted supply chain campaign against crypto wallet developers, including Keplr, Zcash, Vizor, and Cosmos projects. The operator opened malicious pull requests against Chainapsis Vizor and Zingo Labs repositories that tried to exfiltrate CI environment variables and code-signing files. When reviewers caught the payload, the operator added an AGENTS.md rule to talk AI reviewers out of flagging it, then moved the stealer into a Rust crate's build.rs, lwd-uri-util, which ran during every cargo build. The campaign also used a fake security disclosure to phish Vizor maintainers and a Node.js stealer disguised as a git dependency. Defenders should scrutinize build scripts, dependency changes, and AGENTS.md files, and treat secrets in build environments as exposed if affected builds ran.

parsed.title: Beyond the clipboard: The evolving tradecraft of ClickFix
parsed.summary: ClickFix is a social engineering technique that tricks users into pasting and running commands, and threat actors keep finding new ways to use it. Recent campaigns have used malvertising, typosquatted domains, SEO poisoning, and compromised websites to lure victims to fake Cloudflare "verify you are human" pages. Attackers add fake verification messages in terminals to make the malicious PowerShell look legitimate while it downloads and runs payloads. Delivered payloads now include RATs such as a Node.js-based tool disguised as an RMM, lateral movement tooling used to reach domain controllers, and steganographic chains that rebuild executables from PNG files. Defenders should train users never to paste commands at a web page's request, restrict execution from user-writable locations, and monitor for behaviors like browser-spawned PowerShell and new scheduled tasks or Run keys.

parsed.title: Black October 2026: Critical Vulnerabilities, Trusted Technology Under Attack, and What Comes Next
parsed.summary: PHP2Shell, two critical unauthenticated RCE flaws in PHP (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), were rapidly scanned and exploited, and a suspected Chinese-nexus group, CL-UNK-1280, used them with a Linux privilege escalation flaw to compromise about 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS appliances worldwide. October also saw exploitation of BeyondTrust Remote Support and Ivanti Connect Secure, and supply-chain attacks on the LiteLLM package and on 42 GitHub repositories that targeted developer tools and cloud and AI credentials. The report's main takeaway is that the time between disclosure and exploitation is shrinking, so defenders should prioritize by real exposure rather than CVSS alone. It also warns that trusted software, identities, and AI integrations are increasingly used as attack paths. Holiday staffing gaps may heighten ransomware and fraud risk through the end of 2026.

parsed.title: 2026-11-10: Antifox Agentic Pentesting Platform Used to Steal AWS Credentials and Move Laterally in Compromised Environments
parsed.summary: AntiFox, an open source Chinese-language agentic penetration testing platform, was observed in intrusions where Alibaba Cloud systems hosting its interfaces were tied to malicious activity against internet-facing web services and associated AWS environments. In one path, the w3wp.exe process of a compromised IIS server created an ASPX web shell and ran commands that harvested web.config files, database connection strings, and configuration and log files. In other cases, the actor began with a valid AWS credential obtained by unknown means. Using IAM users or an assumed EC2 role, the actor rapidly enumerated dozens of AWS services, and some runs reached a successful GetSecretValue call against a production secret. Defenders should hunt for w3wp.exe spawning shells, new ASPX files in writable directories, and rapid cross-service List, Get, and Describe bursts from novel hosting infrastructure. Rotating exposed credentials and enforcing IMDSv2 and least-privilege policies are key mitigations.

parsed.title: Open up, this is an order: Exploiting CVE-2026-21513 to deliver a JScript backdoor
parsed.summary: PT ESC researchers observed exploitation of CVE-2026-21513, a flaw in the Windows MSHTML component, in attacks against Russian organizations. The attack chain starts with a DOCX file disguised as an official order, which loads a remote RTF document via WebDAV. That RTF references a malicious LNK-plus-HTML file that exploits the vulnerability to launch a DLL loader, which in turn runs mshta.exe to install a JScript backdoor. The backdoor persists through a scheduled task that runs every 30 minutes, reports basic user and domain details to the operator, and executes server-supplied code via eval. Attackers can also deliver a reconnaissance payload that clears Office and IE caches before collecting system information. Defenders should install the February 2026 or later Windows security updates and hunt for the listed artifacts, since patching does not remove an existing infection.

parsed.title: Unpacking a Multi-Stage Loader: From Embedded Payloads to Cobalt Strike Beacon
parsed.summary: Threatcat analysed a multi-stage loader delivered via a SwissTransfer link containing a zip with a malicious Windows shortcut (.lnk) that hides a second payload past the file's end, extracted using curl and tar. The shortcut launches a batch/PowerShell polyglot dropper that displays a decoy "Sample Luxury London Apartment" PDF to the victim while running a fileless .NET loader. Subsequent stages unpack layered XOR and GZip-protected .NET assemblies and a raw x64 shellcode loader, which runs Cobalt Strike's PrependLoader in memory. The final payload is a 64-bit Cobalt Strike Beacon, likely version 4.13 or later, configured for HTTPS C2 over CloudFront on port 443. The lure targets people seeking rental or real-estate listings, and the report notes that the in-memory techniques aim to reduce detection rather than guarantee stealth.

parsed.title: CNCERT: In-Depth Analysis Report on the Attack Landscape of the “Golden Hook (G03)” Group Behind the “Silver Fox” Trojan
parsed.summary: The CNCERT report describes the "Golden Hook (G03)" group, which distributes the Silver Fox trojan through fake Chinese stock trading software sites impersonating Tonghuashun (10jqka), promoted via SEO poisoning. Victims who download the bundled installer are led through multi-stage in-memory loading that ends with a remote-access trojan capable of screenshots, keylogging, command execution, and plugin delivery over TCP. The group targets Chinese universities, healthcare, securities firms, and technology companies. The trojan persists through a user-level Run registry entry and uses an anti-sandbox check based on process count. CNCERT observed 25,164 compromised hosts in China between October 4 and November 2, 2026. Defenders should download software only from official sources and check for the SystemKKfile registry entry and suspicious programs in the Temp directory.
